bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Pay: Hourly to Annual

Whether you are negotiating a salary offer or checking your current wage, converting an hourly rate to an annual figure is straightforward. The basic formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a standard full-time position, we assume 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This gives you a consistent annual estimate. However, your actual hours may vary if you work part-time, overtime, or irregular shifts. Our [the timesheet](/) lets you adjust the weekly hours to match your situation.

### The Formula in Practice

Let’s say you earn $30 per hour. Multiply by 38 hours: $1,140 per week. Multiply by 52 weeks: $59,280 gross per year. That is your annual salary before tax and super. If you are paid fortnightly, your gross pay would be $2,280 (weekly × 2). Many employers quote salaries as annual figures, so this conversion helps you compare offers.

Remember: this calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It is an estimate, not a determination of your pay.

## National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage. From 1 July 2026, it is **$26.44 per hour**, or **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 hours. If you are a casual employee, you receive a 25% loading on top, making the casual minimum **$33.05 per hour**. Many industries have award rates that are higher than the minimum. Check your specific award via the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page or the Fair Work Ombudsman website. Our calculator uses the national minimum as a baseline, but you can enter any hourly rate.

### Casual Loading Explained

Casual loading compensates for the lack of paid leave (annual leave, sick leave) and other entitlements. The standard loading is 25% of the base hourly rate. For example, if your base rate is $26.44, the casual rate is $33.05. When using our [the timesheet](/), tick the “casual loading” checkbox to add 25% on top of the base rate you type. **Never type a rate that already includes casual loading** – the calculator adds it for you. This ensures your annual estimate reflects the correct loaded amount. For more details, see [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).

## Superannuation Paid on Top

Super guarantee is an additional 12% of your ordinary earnings (2026–27 rate), paid by your employer on top of your salary. It is not deducted from your pay. For a $59,280 annual salary, super would be about $7,114, bringing total remuneration to $66,394. The super guarantee has a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year – earnings above that do not attract compulsory super. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary packaging and the super cap work. The calculator estimates super on ordinary earnings only, up to the base.

## What Is Average Salary in Australia?

To understand where your pay sits, look at the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) data. For May 2026, the ABS reported:
- Full-time adult ordinary time earnings: **$2,083.70 per week** (annualised: about $108,352)
- All employees total earnings (including part-time): **$1,579.20 per week** (annualised: about $82,118)

These are **averages**, not medians for a specific job. Your industry or occupation may differ. For example, the average for all employees includes many part-time workers, so it is lower than the full-time figure. Use our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page to explore more data. Remember: “what is average salary in australia” is a common question, and the answer depends on whether you look at full-time, part-time, or all employees. The ABS averages are a useful benchmark, but they do not represent any particular role.

### Tax Considerations

Once you have your annual gross pay, you can estimate tax. The 2026–27 resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (generally). For a $59,280 salary, tax would be approximately $8,367 plus Medicare $1,186, leaving about $49,727 after tax. Our calculator uses these rates with the full tax-free threshold. It does not deduct HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. See [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) for more details.

## Using the Timesheet

Our [the timesheet](/) is the home page where you enter your base hourly rate. You can adjust weekly hours (default 38), add casual loading, and see annual, fortnightly, and monthly figures. The calculator also shows estimated tax and super. It is a tool for quick comparisons, not a binding pay slip. Always consult your employer or a tax professional for precise figures.

### Key Takeaways

- Annual salary = hourly × hours per week × 52 (assume 38 hours for full-time)
- Fortnightly pay = weekly × 2
- National minimum wage: $26.44/hr; casual $33.05/hr
- Super is 12% on top, up to $270,830 earnings
- ABS average full-time weekly earnings: $2,083.70 (May 2026)
- Tax brackets and Medicare apply

For more information, visit our [reference tables](/data) or [pay guides](/blog). The [about the timesheet](/about) page explains the assumptions and limitations. Remember, this is an estimate – your actual pay may vary due to overtime, penalties, or enterprise agreements.
